Subject: Tenant provisioning matrix + egress constraints

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We took your notes back to the networking team and attached a first-pass provisioning matrix (see acme-provisioning-matrix.xlsx). Two specific asks as we plan the integration: 

1) Can you confirm the control-plane endpoint set (FQDNs + ports) we should expect to allow cross-connect/VPN traffic to? We need a short allowlist to share with our NetSec team.

2) For egress: we have compliance constraints that require outbound connections to be routed via customer-controlled egress IPs. Is Redwood able to support a customer-managed NAT egress (we provide IPs) or do we need to use Redwood-managed egress with an allowlist model?

We are looking to start provisioning the first tenant week of Nov 20th and would like a short runbook for the ops handoff.

Attachments: acme-provisioning-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Samir

Samir —

Appreciate the matrix and the clear asks. Copying Kimberly and Karthik to scope the controls and timeline. Quick answers up-front:

- Control plane: we provide a concise allowlist (three FQDNs + 443) — I'll attach our onboarding playbook which lists the exact endpoints and certificate thumbprints.
- Egress: we support both patterns. For regulated customers you can supply customer NAT IPs (cross-connect or VPN + routing) and we will route outbound traffic through those IPs (customer-managed egress), or we can expose a Redwood-managed egress with an allowlist model if that is easier for short-term testing. 

Proposal: 30–45 minute technical workshop this week to lock the matrix and pick egress path. After that we'll produce a short runbook for the ops handoff. Attaching: redwood-tenant-onboarding-playbook.pdf (summary + sample diagrams).

Proposed times: Thu 11/2 10:00–10:45 PST or Fri 11/3 13:00–13:45 PST — which works?

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Tenant provisioning matrix + egress constraints — technical notes

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the matrix. I pulled out the items we need to finalize for a clean handoff. High-level control-plane / data-plane split and reference endpoints below — please confirm that these lines up with what your NetSec team expects.

Control plane (managed by Redwood):
- api.redwood-inference-hosted.example:443 (TLS, mutual TLS optional for dedicated installs)
- auth.redwood-inference-hosted.example:443
- telemetry.redwood-inference-hosted.example:443 (if you enable optional metrics shipping)
- Notes: control-plane traffic is primarily TLS over 443 and originates from REDWOOD control-plane subnets. We can provide CIDR blocks if you prefer IP-level allowlist.

Data plane (tenant workload / inference):
- In private deployments the inference nodes egress directly through customer network (recommended) or via Redwood egress proxy for short-term testing.
- If you provide NAT IPs we will configure route policies to NAT outbound token/metric destinations through those IPs.

Egress options (pros/cons):
- Customer-managed NAT (preferred for compliance): you provide egress IPs / cross-connect; your team retains full egress control. Slightly more work on provisioning.
- Redwood-managed egress (fast to start): we operate an egress proxy; you provide destination allowlists and we provide audit logs. Good for POC.

Operational checklist (what we need from Acme):
- Customer egress IP(s) or confirmation to use Redwood egress (one line)
- Cross-connect ticket / VPN details + ASN if using BGP
- VLAN tagging info and any required MTU settings
- Contact for ops day-of (name + pager)

I'll bring a sample topology diagram to the workshop (simple control-plane / data-plane demarcation) and the exact CIDRs for control plane.

Attachment referenced in thread: acme-provisioning-matrix.xlsx (we updated a few columns)

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant provisioning matrix + egress constraints — rollout timing

Quick timeline note from infra side:

- Workshop this week to finalize matrix (1 session).
- Provisioning sprint (internal): provision network and tenant objects — 3 business days once we have cross-connect/VPN details and egress decision.
- Canary cutover: schedule 3 tenants for a canary group (small traffic) during week-of-Nov-20.
- Full ramp: after successful canary (2–3 business days of validation), we can start staged rollout for additional tenants.

Dependencies that affect dates: signed cross-connect ticket or VPN handoff, and access to routing/security ACLs from Acme. If Acme needs Redwood-managed egress for the POC we can still hit Nov-20 but will need to sign off on audit config.

I'll prepare a short acceptance checklist we can use during the canary window (traffic checks, latency thresholds, metric sanity, and failback plan).

—Karthik

- Egress: Acme has chosen customer-managed NAT IPs for compliance. Acme to provide the NAT IPs and cross-connect details. Redwood will configure routing and NAT on the tenant data-plane to use those IPs.

- Redwood (Kimberly): finalize topology diagram + exact CIDRs and attach to the onboarding runbook — due 11/6.
- Redwood (Karthik): runbook + acceptance checklist for canary — due 11/12.
- Marissa: coordinate scheduling and confirm workshop time — I'll send a calendar invite for Thu 11/2 10:00 PST (if that time no longer works please propose Fri 11/3 13:00 PST).
